ai.literal: To be feared they will not experience, esteem they will lose, always, liquor desire having those who conduct themselves.
ai.translation: Those who live with a constant craving for liquor will never be feared or respected, and they will lose their esteem forever.
ai.modern: கள்ளின் மீது ஆசை கொண்டு வாழ்பவர்கள், மற்றவர்களால் அஞ்சப்படவோ மதிக்கப்படவோ மாட்டார்கள்; அவர்கள் தங்கள் புகழையும் எப்போதும் இழப்பார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns of the social consequences of alcoholism. The phrase 'உட்கப் படாஅர்' means they will not inspire fear or respect in others, making them vulnerable. 'ஒளி இழப்பர்' indicates the loss of their inner light, dignity, and public esteem. Thus, those who live driven by a desire for liquor ('கள் காதல் கொண்டு ஒழுகுவார்') forfeit both their power and their reputation permanently ('எஞ்ஞான்றும்').

ai.literal: Do not drink liquor; if drinking, let drink by the noble to be esteemed those who do not desire.
ai.translation: Do not drink liquor. If it must be drunk, let it be drunk only by those who do not care to be esteemed by the noble.
ai.modern: கள்ளை குடிக்கக் கூடாது; குடிப்பதாக இருந்தால், சான்றோர்களால் மதிக்கப்படுவதை விரும்பாதவர்கள் மட்டும் குடிக்கட்டும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet issues a strict command against consuming intoxicating liquor. It then uses a rhetorical concession, stating that if someone insists on drinking, it should only be those who do not care about their reputation. The phrase 'சான்றோரான் எண்ணப்பட வேண்டாதார்' refers to people who have no desire to be respected among the wise and noble. By framing it this way, the poet emphasizes that drinking liquor completely destroys one's standing among virtuous people.

ai.literal: Even in the presence of the mother who bore one, it is unpleasant; what then of intoxication in the presence of the noble?
ai.translation: Drunkenness is painful even in the presence of one's own mother. How much worse will it be before the wise?
ai.modern: பெற்ற தாயின் முன்னிலையிலும் குடிப்பழக்கம் துன்பம் தருவதாகும்; அப்படியிருக்க, சான்றோர்களின் முன்னிலையில் குடித்து மயங்குவது பற்றி என்ன சொல்வது?
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the universal disgrace of drunkenness. A mother's love is naturally forgiving and unconditional, yet even she finds her child's intoxication painful and repulsive. The poet uses this extreme example to ask a rhetorical question: if even a mother cannot bear the sight of drunkenness, how much more offensive will it be to the wise and noble, who judge by virtue and reason? The word 'களி' (intoxication) is contrasted with the presence of 'சான்றோர்' (the noble) to emphasize the incompatibility of vice and virtue.

ai.literal: Modesty called good woman back will give toddy called unesteemed to those with great fault.
ai.translation: The good woman called Modesty will turn her back on those who commit the despised, great fault of drinking toddy.
ai.modern: கள் குடித்தல் என்னும் விரும்பத்தகாத பெரிய குற்றத்தைச் செய்பவர்களை விட்டு, நாணம் என்று சொல்லப்படும் நல்லவள் விலகிச் செல்வாள்.
ai.explanation: The poet personifies modesty as a noble woman who refuses to associate with drunkards. Drinking toddy is described as a great, unesteemed fault that strips a person of their sense of shame. By turning her back, Modesty abandons the drunkard entirely, leaving them without dignity or moral standing.

ai.literal: Proper conduct ignorance it possesses indeed, wealth having given, body ignorance acquiring.
ai.translation: Spending wealth to acquire a state of bodily unawareness is an act of utter senselessness.
ai.modern: பணத்தைக் கொடுத்துத் தன் உடலையே அறியாத மயக்க நிலையை விலைக்கு வாங்குவது, என்ன செய்வதென்று அறியாத பெரும் முட்டாள்தனமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet points out the absurdity of paying for one's own intoxication. The phrase 'பொருள் கொடுத்து' means spending valuable wealth, while 'மெய்யறியாமை கொளல்' refers to buying a drunken state where one loses awareness of their own physical body. The poet concludes that doing this shows a complete lack of basic sense or proper conduct, expressed by the word 'கை' which here signifies proper action or what one ought to do.

ai.literal: Those who sleep than the dead different are not; always poison those who eat [are] liquor those who consume.
ai.translation: Those who sleep are no different from the dead. Those who drink liquor are, at all times, simply drinking poison.
ai.modern: தூங்குபவர்கள் இறந்தவர்களை விட வேறுபட்டவர்கள் அல்லர். அதுபோலவே, கள் குடிப்பவர்கள் எப்போதும் நஞ்சு உண்பவர்களே ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: The couplet compares sleep to death, noting that a sleeping person is temporarily unaware like a corpse. It then draws a parallel to drinking liquor, stating that those who consume alcohol are essentially consuming poison. The word 'எஞ்ஞான்றும்' (always) emphasizes that drinking is inherently destructive at all times.

ai.literal: Inside having hidden, by the local town they will be laughed at, always, liquor having hidden eyes those who droop.
ai.translation: Those who secretly drink liquor and let their intoxicated eyes droop will always be laughed at by the whole town, even if they think they are hiding it inside.
ai.modern: கள்ளை மறைத்துக் குடித்துவிட்டுப் போதையால் கண்கள் சொருகுபவர்கள், தாங்கள் குடித்ததை மனத்திற்குள் மறைத்தாலும், உள்ளூர் மக்களால் எக்காலத்தும் சிரிக்கப்படுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet mocks the foolishness of secret drinkers. The word 'ஒற்றி' (from 'ஒற்றுதல்') is used here in the sense of hiding or concealing. A person might consume liquor in secret and try to hide the fact in their mind ('உள் ஒற்றி'). However, the physical effects of intoxication, such as drooping eyes, cannot be concealed. Consequently, their secret is exposed, and they become a constant laughingstock to the people of their town.

ai.literal: Having been intoxicated I know not, saying that let one abandon; in the heart even that which was hidden right there will increase.
ai.translation: Let one give up saying, "I have never known intoxication." When drunk, even the secrets hidden deep in the heart will readily reveal themselves.
ai.modern: நான் குடித்து அறியமாட்டேன் என்று சொல்வதைக் கைவிட வேண்டும். குடித்தால், மனத்திற்குள் மறைத்து வைத்திருந்த ரகசியங்களும் அப்போதே வெளிப்பட்டுவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the self-deception of a drinker who claims they have never been intoxicated. The word 'kaḷittu' specifically means being intoxicated by drink in this chapter's context. The poet points out that alcohol strips away inhibitions, so 'oḷittatūum' (even hidden things) in the mind will 'mikum' (increase or become manifest) right then and there. Thus, trying to hide one's drinking is futile, as the drink itself will force the truth out.

ai.literal: To an intoxicated man reason showing, under water to a submerged man fire having searched like that.
ai.translation: Trying to reason with a drunkard is like searching with a torch for a man who has sunk underwater.
ai.modern: குடிபோதையில் இருப்பவனுக்கு நியாயங்களை எடுத்துக் கூறுவது, தண்ணீருக்கு அடியில் மூழ்கியவனைத் தீப்பந்தம் கொண்டு தேடுவதற்குச் சமமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a striking simile to illustrate the futility of arguing with someone who is drunk. The word 'களித்தானை' refers to an intoxicated person whose mind is completely clouded. Trying to show them 'காரணம்' (reason or logic) is compared to searching for someone who has submerged 'கீழ் நீர்' (under water) using 'தீ' (fire or a torch). Just as a torch is extinguished underwater and cannot illuminate the depths, logic and reason cannot penetrate a mind submerged in intoxication.

ai.literal: liquor not-drinking at-the-time intoxicated-man-(acc.) seeing when he-does-not-think I-wonder of-having-drunk stupor
ai.translation: When a man who is currently sober sees someone who is intoxicated, does he not realize the shameful stupor his own drinking causes?
ai.modern: தான் மது அருந்தாத நேரத்தில், மது அருந்தி மயங்கியிருப்பவனைப் பார்க்கும் ஒருவன், தான் மது அருந்தியதால் ஏற்படும் மயக்கத்தையும் சோர்வையும் பற்றி நினைக்க மாட்டானோ?
ai.explanation: The couplet asks a rhetorical question about self-awareness and the loss of dignity caused by intoxication. It observes a person who drinks but is currently sober, watching another person who is completely drunk. The word 'சோர்வு' (cōrvu) captures the physical weakness, loss of senses, and resulting disgrace of drunkenness. By seeing the foolish state of another drunkard, the sober observer should naturally reflect on his own shameful behavior when he drinks.
